chunks: And Ḥammād narrated from al-Ḥalabī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who buys fruit and then sells it before taking possession of it. He said: “There is no harm in it; if he finds profit in it, then let him sell.”

He said: And he عليه السلام was asked about purchasing palm trees, grapevines, and fruits for three years or four. He said: “There is no harm in it. You may say: if it does not come forth in this year, it will come forth in the next. But if you buy it for one year, then do not buy it until it matures.”

He said: And he عليه السلام was asked about a man who buys specified fruit from a land, and then all the fruit of that land perishes. So he said: “They had disputed about that before the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and they used to mention that matter. So when he saw that they would not leave off disputation, he forbade them from that sale until the fruit matures. He did not make it haram, but rather he did that because of their disputation.”

key_terms.الثَّمَرَةَ: fruit produce being bought and sold
key_terms.النَّخْلِ: date-palms as an example of orchard produce
key_terms.الْخُصُومَةَ: disputation or quarrelling that led to restriction of the sale
key_terms.الْكَرْمِ: grapevines mentioned in agricultural sale contracts
key_terms.تَبْلُغَ: to reach maturity, the threshold mentioned for valid one-year purchase
key_terms.شِرَاءِ: the act of purchase in a legal transaction

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling or buying fruit before taking possession of it or before it matures in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses legal rulings related to the sale of fruits before possession and before full maturity. It permits resale when profit is found, allows multi-year purchase of orchard produce, and explains that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم restricted certain fruit-sales before maturity to prevent dispute, not as an absolute prohibition.
